data.one_liner: Declarative API for creating and verifying file and directory structures in tests.
data.what_it_does: Provides an API using descriptors (such as `d.file` and `d.dir`) to declare filesystem structures. It automatically manages a temporary sandbox directory per test, allowing you to create files on disk and validate that file hierarchies match expected structures. It handles setup and cleanup of sandbox directories automatically when used with the `test` package.
use_when: Testing CLI tools, file parsers, or code generators that manipulate filesystem paths
Setting up and validating complex directory and file hierarchies in unit and integration tests
You need isolated sandbox environments per test run that are cleaned up automatically
avoid_when: Testing in environments without `dart:io` access such as web applications
Unit tests that do not involve filesystem interactions
strengths: Declarative, tree-like structure makes complex folder setups easy to read and maintain
Automatic creation and teardown of the temporary test sandbox directory
Provides both creation (`create()`) and assertion (`validate()`) workflows
weaknesses: Archive support (zip/tar) was removed in version 2.0.0
Relies directly on filesystem I/O rather than an in-memory mock filesystem

alternatives.name: file
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides a full mockable filesystem interface (MemoryFileSystem) to test file operations in-memory without touching disk.
